math_plain: Identifying and measuring failure modes in generative systems used for information retrieval.
why_math: It works because vulnerabilities are patterns that emerge when you actually run the system against adversarial or biased inputs—testing whether the system's behavior matches its intended function reveals when it fails.

math_tags: ranking things by a learned score
matching and allocating who gets what
math_plain: Scoring agents by their relevance across multiple criteria—capabilities, behaviors, constraints—and ranking to surface the best fit for each task.
why_math: It works because you only need to order agents correctly by fitness, not predict perfect scores; a rough multi-criterion ranking that gets the best agents on top already solves the discovery problem.

math_tags: measuring similarity as nearness in a space
weighting the parts that are most relevant
math_plain: Extracting user preferences and intents as summaries from language, then using them to personalize search results and recommendations.
why_math: It works because users who express similar preferences tend to want similar results; if you capture what each user cares about, matching new queries to their profile becomes a nearness problem.

math_tags: finding the settings with least error
combining many weak signals into a strong one
math_plain: Defining and measuring correctness when systems generate or retrieve content across text, images, and other modalities simultaneously.
why_math: It works because no single metric captures all aspects of goodness; combining multiple evaluation signals—fidelity, alignment, coherence—gives a fuller picture than any one measure alone.
